newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 industrial employment down 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 industrial employment down 11.1 pct.

text.p: Brazilian industrial employment dropped 11.1 percent in 1996 against previous year levels and fell 1.3 percent in December against November, the National Statistics Institute said in a statement.
The IBGE statement said December employment levels dropped 7.2 percent over a 12-month period.
The statement said the drop in industrial employment upholds a seven-year trend. The number of workers employed between 1989 and 1996 fell by 34.3 percent.
Manufacturing sectors in Sao Paulo, Brazil's economic powerhouse, showed the biggest decrease in employment in 1996, the IBGE statement said.
It pointed to the clothing, textile and mechanicals industries as those which had been most seriously hurt by a flood of foreign imports.

The IBGE said the drop in employment levels was a nationwide trend seen in all major industrial regions including Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais and the three Southern states of Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and Parana.
The statement said total salaries in the industrial sector fell 7.4 percent in 1996. However, wage income per worker rose 3.4 percent in the year.
Last week, the IBGE reported the Brazilian economy grew 2.9 percent in 1996. A recent poll of Sao Paulo business leaders showed they expect the economy to grow around 4 percent in 1997.
